    payloads[domain] = composer.safeFallbackPayload(
        domain: domain,

title: Turning raw-media retention off does not stop new scans from persisting palm photos
evidence: runPipeline() unconditionally records `scanImagePath = "scans/$monthKey",` (line 487) and captureCurrentAngle() unconditionally writes every accepted frame to `File(appContext.filesDir, "scans/$monthKey")` (lines 196-199). `grep -rn rawMediaRetention app/src data-room/src` returns hits only in SettingsViewModel.kt:54/106/109, SettingsScreen.kt:145, ScanImageCleanupWorker.kt:45 and Entities.kt:19 — ScanViewModel never reads the flag. With the switch OFF, SettingsViewModel.setRetention() (line 111) deletes only the images that already exist; every subsequent scan re-creates them and they survive until ScanImageCleanupWorker next runs, which PalmAstroApp.kt:72-73 schedules as `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<ScanImageCleanupWorker>(6, TimeUnit.HOURS).setInitialDelay(1, TimeUnit.HOURS)` — i.e. up to ~6h later, longer under Doze/battery batching. The shipped policy at app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy_en.html:65 states verbatim: "You can turn off photo retention in Settings, in which case scan photos are not kept after analysis." PRD §15 ("User can disable raw media retention") and §58 ("Privacy policy matches actual behavior") are both violated.
userImpact: A privacy-conscious user who switches raw-media retention off is told photos are not kept after analysis, but every new scan leaves seven full-resolution palm photos in app storage for up to six hours. The in-app privacy policy — and the same text at the public policy URL required by the Play launch gate — is factually wrong about the app's behavior.

title: Turning off photo retention does not stop new scans from writing palm photos to disk
evidence: `val scanDir = File(appContext.filesDir, "scans/$monthKey")` / `scanDir.mkdirs()` / `val outputFile = File(scanDir, "${angle.name}.jpg")` (lines 196-198) — every captured angle is written to internal storage unconditionally, and `runPipeline()` then persists `scanImagePath = "scans/$monthKey",` (line 487). Neither the capture path nor the pipeline ever reads `profile.rawMediaRetention`. A repo-wide grep for `rawMediaRetention` in app/src/main/kotlin returns only SettingsViewModel.kt (24, 54, 106, 109) and ScanImageCleanupWorker.kt (45-46). `SettingsViewModel.setRetention(false)` (line 110-112) calls `wipeManager.deleteAllScanImages()`, which deletes only photos that *already* exist; photos captured *after* the toggle is off are written and left in place until the periodic worker runs. That worker is scheduled in PalmAstroApp.kt:71-80 with `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<ScanImageCleanupWorker>(6, TimeUnit.HOURS).setInitialDelay(1, TimeUnit.HOURS)`, so the photos survive on disk for at least an hour and typically hours more. The bundled policy states the opposite at app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy_en.html:65: `You can turn off photo retention in Settings, in which case scan photos are not kept after analysis.` (zh-TW equivalent at privacy_policy_zh-TW.html:65). docs/store/play/permissions.md:17-18 repeats the claim to Play reviewers: "Raw photos auto-delete within 24 hours by default; retention can be disabled entirely."
userImpact: A privacy-conscious user explicitly disables photo retention, scans their palm, and their palm photographs sit in app storage for hours anyway — recoverable by device forensics, an ADB backup attempt, or anyone with the unlocked phone. The setting the policy sells as "not kept after analysis" does nothing for the scan the user just took.

1. `ScanViewModel.captureCurrentAngle()` (app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/viewmodel/ScanViewModel.kt:194-198) builds `File(appContext.filesDir, "scans/$monthKey")`, `mkdirs()`, and writes `${angle.name}.jpg` via CameraX with no retention check. 4. `SettingsViewModel.setRetention(false)` (105-114) only calls `wipeManager.deleteAllScanImages()`, and `WipeManager.deleteScanImages()` (WipeManager.kt:42-45) is a one-shot `scansDir.deleteRecursively()` — retroactive only, no standing enforcement.

Real-world delay is >= 1h and, because KEEP preserves an existing schedule whose window may have just elapsed, typically up to ~6h, longer under Doze.
6. The shipped policy contradicts this at app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy_en.html:65 ("scan photos are not kept after analysis") and :24, so this is a stated-policy/data-safety mismatch, not just an internal nit.

That still warrants high for a privacy-first launch.

The proposed fix is also partly wrong: `ResultRepository` (data-room/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/data/repository/ResultRepository.kt) exposes no `clearScanImagePathForMonth` — that method exists only on `MonthlyResultDao`, used by the worker. title: Onboarding birthday validation error is silent to TalkBack — no liveRegion, no error semantics
evidence:
L376-379:
```
errorRes?.let {
    Spacer(Modifier.height(8.dp))
    Text(stringResource(it), color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
}
```
The error is set only inside the Next-button lambda at L381-389 (`errorRes = R.string.ob_birthday_future` / `R.string.ob_birthday_invalid`). The Text carries no `liveRegion`, no `semantics { error(...) }`, and no association with the three dropdowns at L322-355; focus stays on the button, and the text renders above it. The app already uses the correct idiom elsewhere — ScanScreen.kt:399 `modifier = Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite; heading() }`, DomainDetailScreen.kt:119, GuidanceScreen.kt:112 — so this is an omission, not a house style. Birthday is the one required onboarding field, so this is the only blocking validation in the flow (WCAG 3.3.1 / 4.1.3).
fix:
In app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/onboarding/OnboardingScreen.kt, add the two imports alongside the existing androidx.compose.ui.semantics.* imports at L24-28:

    import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.LiveRegionMode
    import androidx.compose.ui.semantics.liveRegion

Then change L399 (inside the errorRes?.let block at L397-400) from:

    Text(stringResource(it), color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)

to:

    Text(
        stringResource(it),
        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,
        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
        modifier = Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Assertive },
    )

Assertive rather than the Polite used on the sibling screens is correct here: those announce ambient status, whereas this blocks the user from advancing and should interrupt. Note that androidx.compose.ui.semantics.error() is NOT applicable — it attaches to a text-field node, and the three birthday inputs are OutlinedButton + DropdownMenu, not text fields, so liveRegion is the whole fix. Optionally also prefix the announcement with the field name so the user knows which of the three dropdowns to correct.
userImpact: A TalkBack user who picks 31 February or a future birthday taps Next and hears absolutely nothing. The screen appears frozen and they have no way to learn why onboarding will not advance.
verifierNote: Confirmed by reading OnboardingScreen.kt in full. The error Text (actually at L397-400, not the claimed L376-379 — line numbers drifted, content matches verbatim) carries no liveRegion and no semantics of any kind. Refutation attempts all failed: (1) grep for liveRegion across app/src/main/kotlin returns only GuidanceScreen.kt:112, ScanScreen.kt:361/399, DomainDetailScreen.kt:119 — nothing in the onboarding package; there is also no announceForAccessibility, no AccessibilityManager, and no SnackbarHost anywhere in ui/onboarding/, so nothing else announces it. Compose emits no TalkBack event for a newly-composed node, and focus remains on the Button tapped at L402. (2) Both error branches are genuinely reachable: the day dropdown at L365 offers (1..31) for every month regardless of selMonth, so 31 February throws DateTimeException and sets ob_birthday_invalid at L408; the year dropdown at L373 is (currentYear downTo 1930), so selecting 2026 with a month/day after today trips d.isAfter(LocalDate.now()) at L405. Both strings exist in values/ and values-zh-rTW/strings_onboarding.xml. (3) Not house style — three sibling screens use the exact idiom for status text, so this is an omission. Two corrections to the auditor: the WCAG cite is half wrong (this is 4.1.3 Status Messages, AA — 3.3.1 Error Identification, A, is arguably met since the error text does exist in the tree and renders above the button inside the scrollable column, so it is reachable by backwards swipe), and the impact claim 'no way to learn why' is therefore overstated; what is accurate is that tapping Next produces zero audible feedback, leaving no cue that anything changed or that the user should go looking. Severity high stands: onboarding is the mandatory first-run flow and birthday is its only blocking validation.

title: Dark mode: every content card renders at exactly the page background hex
evidence: DarkColorScheme sets `background = Color(0xFF1C1B1F)` (line 60) and `surface = Color(0xFF1C1B1F)` (line 62) — the identical value — and defines no surfaceContainer* roles, so `surfaceContainerLow` falls back to the M3 1.2.1 baseline PaletteTokens.Neutral10, which I verified by disassembling material3-release.aar is rgb(28,27,31) = #1C1B1F, the same hex a third time. Every content card is therefore invisible in dark mode: ResultsScreen.kt:386 `containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface` (GuidanceEntryCard) and ResultsScreen.kt:509 (DomainCardItem) — both with `elevation = CardDefaults.cardElevation(defaultElevation = 0.dp)` and no border; DomainDetailScreen.kt:383 `containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainerLow` (ScoreEducationCard); ExplainabilityScreen.kt:106 (baseline card). Scaffold's default container is `colorScheme.background`, and since the container color equals `colorScheme.surface`, Surface's tonal-elevation lift is 0.dp, so nothing separates card from page. The only remaining cue on the home screen is the 3.dp progress line at ResultsScreen.kt:523.
fix: In Theme.kt DarkColorScheme: change line 60 to `background = Color(0xFF121116)`, keep `surface = Color(0xFF1C1B1F)` as the card ground, and add `surfaceContainerLow = Color(0xFF221F27)`, `surfaceContainerHigh = Color(0xFF2B2830)`, plus `outlineVariant = Color(0xFF423F49)`. That alone is not sufficient: #1C1B1F on #121116 is only a 1.10:1 luminance ratio, the same razor-thin gap M3 itself uses -- but M3 backs it with default card shadow elevation, which this app explicitly zeroes at every site. So also give the four zero-elevation cards a hairline edge: add `border = BorderStroke(1.dp, MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outlineVariant)` to the Cards at ResultsScreen.kt:380 (GuidanceEntryCard) and :492 (DomainCardItem), and to DomainDetailScreen.kt:383 and ExplainabilityScreen.kt:105. The border is theme-safe in light mode too (light outlineVariant reads as a soft grey hairline), so it needs no dark-only branch. `surfaceContainerHighest` is not referenced by any app code -- only M3 text fields/sliders consume it internally -- so adding it is optional polish. The LightColorScheme addition of `surfaceContainerLow = Color(0xFFF3EDFB)` is a brand-tint nicety, not a defect fix: the light baseline is Neutral96 #F7F2FA (not #F7F2F7) and already separates from background #FFFBFF.
userImpact: On a dark-theme phone the Results home screen and the two "understand your score" cards lose all structure — text blocks float on an unbroken black field with no card edges, which reads as an unfinished screen rather than a premium one.
verifierNote: Verified end to end, including the bytecode claim. Theme.kt:60 background=#1C1B1F and :62 surface=#1C1B1F are identical, and DarkColorScheme overrides no surfaceContainer* role. Disassembling material3-release.aar 1.2.1 (the version Compose BOM 2024.06.00 resolves, app/build.gradle.kts:122): PaletteTokens.Neutral10 <clinit> pushes bipush 28/27/31 -> #1C1B1F, and ColorDarkTokens sets both Surface and SurfaceContainerLow to Neutral10. So background, surface, and surfaceContainerLow all resolve to #1C1B1F -- card-to-page contrast exactly 1.00:1. All four call sites check out: ResultsScreen.kt:384 (GuidanceEntryCard) and :495 (DomainCardItem) both use containerColor=colorScheme.surface with elevation=CardDefaults.cardElevation(defaultElevation=0.dp) and no border; DomainDetailScreen.kt:383 and ExplainabilityScreen.kt:105 use surfaceContainerLow. FilledCardTokens.ContainerElevation = ElevationTokens.Level0 = 0.dp, so the latter two get no shadow and no tonal lift either. Scaffold at ResultsScreen.kt:83 passes no containerColor, so it defaults to colorScheme.background. No border/Divider/page gradient exists anywhere in ResultsScreen (the only Brush at :277 is the transparent constellation panel), so the 3.dp LinearProgressIndicator really is the last remaining edge cue. MainActivity.kt:46 calls PalmAstroTheme { } with darkTheme defaulting to isSystemInDarkTheme(), so this reaches any dark-theme device. Refutation attempts that failed: tonal elevation cannot rescue it (elevation is 0 at every site); dynamicColor is hard-off; light mode is unaffected (background #FFFBFF vs baseline surfaceContainerLow #F7F2FA). Corrected severity to high rather than blocker: nothing crashes or loses data, onSurface #E6E1E5 on #1C1B1F is ~13:1 so all text stays readable, and the cards remain identifiable by text and chevron, so there is no hard WCAG 1.4.11 failure -- it is a severe visual-hierarchy defect, not a functional one. Also corrected the fix: the proposed background #121116 gives only 1.10:1 against the #1C1B1F card (luminances 0.005869 vs 0.011308), which merely matches M3's own baseline gap -- and M3 pairs that gap with default card shadow elevation, which this app zeroes at all four sites, so a hairline border is required for the fix to actually read. title: Fixed `.height()` on four text buttons clips the label at large font scales
evidence:
ResultsScreen.kt:218 `OutlinedButton(onClick = onScanClick, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).height(48.dp), shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)) {`
ResultsScreen.kt:221 the identical `.weight(1f).height(48.dp)` for the History button
ResultsScreen.kt:252 `Button(onClick = onScanClick, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(0.7f).height(56.dp), shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)) {`
DomainDetailScreen.kt:225 `modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(48.dp),`
`Modifier.height()` pins min == max. Button content padding is `ButtonDefaults.ContentPadding` = 8.dp top + 8.dp bottom, so the 48.dp buttons leave 32.dp for text. The label style is `labelLarge` (14sp / 20sp lineHeight); at the 2.0x accessibility font scale that line box is 40dp against 32dp available, so the glyphs are cut off. Every other button in the codebase uses the safe idiom — OnboardingScreen.kt:184 `.heightIn(min = 54.dp)`, ScanScreen.kt:406 `.heightIn(min = 48.dp)`, JournalScreen.kt:113 `.heightIn(min = 48.dp)` — and GuidanceScreen.kt:328 even carries the comment "Min-size (not fixed) so the step number never clips at large font scales."
fix: Swap the fixed heights for minimums so the touch-target floor is kept and the buttons grow instead of clipping: ResultsScreen.kt:218 and :221 `Modifier.weight(1f).heightIn(min = 48.dp)`; ResultsScreen.kt:247 (the auditor cited 252) `Modifier.fillMaxWidth(0.7f).heightIn(min = 56.dp)`; and app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/detail/DomainDetailScreen.kt:225 (not ui/results/) `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(min = 48.dp)`. Note the two Rescan/History buttons also wrap to two lines at 2.0x inside their weight(1f) halves, so heightIn alone is what makes the wrapped label visible — no maxLines/ellipsis should be added, since that would trade clipping for truncation.
userImpact: At Android's largest font setting the "Rescan", "History", "Start scan" and "Write in journal" labels are sliced horizontally. Users who need large text — the ones most likely to have turned it on — cannot read the two buttons that lead out of the results screen.
verifierNote: Confirmed by reading the code. Theme.kt:129 copies stock Typography() and its own comment states labelLarge stays stock (14sp/20sp), so the auditor's line-box math is right. There is no font-scale clamp anywhere in the app module — the only `fontScale` use is ScoreGauge.kt:68 for gauge diameter, and MainActivity has no attachBaseContext/Configuration override — so a 2.0x system setting reaches these composables unmodified. ButtonDefaults.ContentPadding is 8dp top/bottom for both Button and OutlinedButton, leaving 32dp inside the 48dp buttons against a ~40dp line box; Compose clamps the Text node to the constraint and clipRects the overflow (hasVisualOverflow path), so glyphs are genuinely cut, not overdrawn. The real-world damage is worse than described because the labels also wrap: 重新掃描 (values-zh-rTW/strings.xml:82) is ~112dp at 28sp inside a weight(1f) column that leaves ~112dp after 48dp of horizontal content padding on a 360dp screen, and English "Scan Again" is wider — it wraps to two lines (80dp) into 32dp, so the second line disappears entirely. Same for 開始掃描掌紋 in the 56dp button (~192dp needed vs ~159dp available), which is why it clips even though its 40dp line box exactly matches its 40dp of interior space. The comparison set checks out: a repo-wide grep shows these four are the only fixed-height buttons left; every other one uses heightIn(min=), including ResultsScreen.kt:384 in the same file, and GuidanceScreen.kt:326 documents the rationale. Two corrections to the write-up, neither of which undermines it: the DomainDetailScreen path is app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/detail/DomainDetailScreen.kt (not ui/results/), and the third ResultsScreen site is line 247, not 252.

title: iOS renders raw English engine grades ('Growing'/'Watchout') where Android localizes them — zh-Hant is the launch language
evidence:
ScoreGaugeView.swift:81 renders the grade with the explicitly non-localizing initializer:
```
Text(verbatim: grade)
```
and ios/App/Results/ResultsView.swift:131 uses the `StringProtocol` overload, which is also non-localizing because `grade` is a `String` variable, not a literal key:
```
Text(payload.scoreCard.grade).font(.subheadline).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
```
The values come straight from default-ruleset.json gradeThresholds: "Growing", "Stable", "Building", "Watchout". Neither ios/App/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable.strings nor zh-Hant.lproj/Localizable.strings contains any `grade_*` key (`grep -n "grade"` returns only `gauge_a11y_format` at line 195/193). Android localizes every occurrence via app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/LocalizedHelpers.kt:8-14 `gradeNameLocalized`, backed by app/src/main/res/values-zh-rTW/strings.xml:7-10: `成長期 / 穩定期 / 累積期 / 注意期` (and values/strings.xml:5-8 `Growing / Stable / Building / Watch Out` — note Android's English is 'Watch Out', two words, while iOS shows the raw token 'Watchout'). The unlocalized string also reaches VoiceOver through ScoreGaugeView.swift:106-111, which interpolates `grade` into `gauge_a11y_format`.
userImpact: A Traditional-Chinese user — the launch audience — sees the hero gauge and every one of the four domain cards labelled with the raw English token 'Watchout' / 'Growing' in an otherwise fully Chinese screen, and VoiceOver reads the same untranslated token. The identical screen on Android reads 注意期 / 成長期.
verifierNote: Confirmed on every claim. ScoreCard.grade is `public let grade: String` (CoreContracts/Models.swift:279,431) populated from raw ruleset keys (ScoringEngineImpl.swift:66 -> Ruleset.grade(forScore:) -> default-ruleset.json:29-34 "Watchout"/"Building"/"Stable"/"Growing"). ScoreGaugeView.swift:81 uses `Text(verbatim: grade)` (explicitly non-localizing) and ResultsView.swift:131 uses `Text(payload.scoreCard.grade)` which binds to the StringProtocol overload, also non-localizing, because grade is a variable and not a literal. ScoreGaugeView.swift:106-111 interpolates the same raw token into gauge_a11y_format for VoiceOver. Neither en.lproj nor zh-Hant.lproj Localizable.strings contains any grade_* key (grep "grade" hits only gauge_a11y_format at en:195). zh-Hant is a real shipping localization: ios/project.yml declares CFBundleLocalizations [en, zh-Hant] and zh-Hant.lproj/Localizable.strings is fully translated. Android does localize: LocalizedHelpers.kt:9-15 gradeNameLocalized -> values-zh-rTW/strings.xml:7-10 (成長期/穩定期/累積期/注意期), reached from GradePalette.kt:50. Refutation attempts that failed: (a) the content engine DOES hold localized grade labels in content-templates.json labels.grades (zh-TW 成長/穩定/累積/留意) but only ToneRendererImpl.swift:32 consumes them for report body text — nothing localizes ScoreCard.grade on the path to these three views; (b) AppModel.swift:217 also passes grade but as a monthTheme dictionary key, correctly raw, so it is not a fourth defect site. Net: three genuine render sites (hero gauge, domain detail gauge, four domain cards) plus VoiceOver show the raw English token on an otherwise fully Chinese screen in the launch locale. Severity high is right — it is not a crash or data issue, but it is on the primary results screen in the primary launch language and breaks Android parity.

title: Moon ecliptic longitude uses a different truncated series on each platform — same birth data yields a different ASTRO_MOON element and different scores
evidence:
Kotlin `AstroMath.moonEclipticLongitudeDeg` (engine-astro/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/astro/AstroMath.kt:56-77) uses LINEAR mean elements and exactly 6 periodic terms, with no eccentricity damping:
```
val meanLongitude = normalizeDegrees(218.3164477 + 481267.88123421 * t)
...
val longitude = meanLongitude + 6.288774*sin(mp) + 1.274027*sin(2*d-mp) + 0.658314*sin(2*d)
    + 0.213618*sin(2*mp) - 0.185116*sin(m) - 0.114332*sin(2*f)
```
Swift `Astronomy.moonEclipticLongitude` (Astronomy.swift:49-82) uses FULL polynomial mean elements plus 4 extra periodic terms plus an eccentricity factor `e`:
```
let lp = 218.3164477 + 481267.88123421*t - 0.0015786*t*t + t*t*t/538841.0 - t*t*t*t/65194000.0
let e  = 1.0 - 0.002516*t - 0.0000074*t*t
...
sumL += -0.185116 * e * sin(mR)          // e-damped; Kotlin has no e
sumL +=  0.058793 * sin(2*dR - 2*mpR)    // absent in Kotlin
sumL +=  0.057066 * e * sin(2*dR - mR - mpR)  // absent in Kotlin
sumL +=  0.053322 * sin(2*dR + mpR)      // absent in Kotlin
sumL +=  0.045758 * e * sin(2*dR - mR)   // absent in Kotlin
```
I reimplemented both verbatim and swept 12,784 daily L2 birth datetimes (1970-01-01..2004-12-31, 09:00, lon 121.5E, Taipei): max |longitude| difference 0.2142 deg, and the resolved moon SIGN ELEMENT differs on 24 of them (0.19%). Concrete cases: 1973-02-09 -> Kotlin 29.9957 deg = ARIES/FIRE, Swift 30.0786 deg = TAURUS/EARTH; 1980-03-15 -> Kotlin 330.063 deg = PISCES/WATER, Swift 329.9256 deg = AQUARIUS/AIR. Because the element picks the ruleset signal (default-ruleset.json lines 20-23: ASTRO_MOON_FIRE careerWeight 0.5 vs ASTRO_MOON_WATER careerWeight 0.1), the four domain scores diverge for these users. (The Julian Day inputs are provably identical — I verified jd_kotlin == jd_swift == 2448057.7666666666 for 1990-06-15 14:30 at lon 121.5.)
fix:
The auditor's direction is right — the Swift series is the correct Meeus Table 47.A top-10 truncation (I checked each added row: (2,0,-2,0)=0.058793, (2,-1,-1,0)=0.057066, (2,0,1,0)=0.053322, (2,-1,0,0)=0.045758, with `e` correctly applied to exactly the M-exponent-1 terms), so port Swift -> Kotlin rather than the reverse. Two corrections to the proposed patch:

1. Do NOT keep the `normalizeDegrees(...)` wrappers on the mean elements when adding the polynomial terms. They are harmless for sin() but they change nothing while making the two sources visually non-comparable; drop them so the Kotlin expressions can be diffed line-for-line against Astronomy.swift:53-62, and mirror the operator order exactly (`t * t * t / 538841.0`, not `t.pow(3) / 538841.0`) since a different association can shift the last ULP.

2. Replace `Math.toRadians(x)` with an explicit `x * PI / 180.0` helper in this function. The JDK implements `Math.toRadians` as `angdeg / 180.0 * PI` whereas Swift computes `deg * .pi / 180.0` — a different rounding order. That is ~1e-16 deg and irrelevant to the sign 99.999% of the time, but if the goal is a byte-identical series it has to match too.

Then add the missing coverage. `ios/shared-fixtures/` has no astro category at all, so create `ios/shared-fixtures/astro/` (and the corresponding loader arm in ios/PalmAstroKit/Tests/ParityTests/ParityTests.swift, which currently only handles scoring/content/guidance) with Android-generated `AstroResult` fixtures. Include all six cusp cases my sweep surfaced, not just the auditor's two: 1972-11-23, 1973-02-09, 1973-05-02, 1975-03-25, 1979-10-07, 1980-03-15 (09:00, lat 25.0, lon 121.5) — each lands within 0.08 deg of a 30-deg boundary and pins both the moon longitude and the resolved ASTRO_MOON_* signal id.

Worth flagging separately (out of scope for this finding, do not fold it into the same patch): the ascendant latitude clamp also differs — AstroMath.ascendantDegrees coerces to +/-89.9 (AstroMath.kt:105) while Astronomy.ascendantLongitude clamps to +/-66.5 (Astronomy.swift:95). That is a second, independent ASTRO_ASC_* parity divergence for any birth place above 66.5 deg latitude.
userImpact: Roughly 1 in 530 users who supply birth time + place get a different moon element, hence different career/wealth/family/health scores and a different set of explainability rows, depending on whether they open PalmAstro on Android or iOS. The PRD requires the two platforms to produce identical results.
verifierNote:
Confirmed by reading both files and re-deriving the numbers independently. `AstroMath.moonEclipticLongitudeDeg` (engine-astro/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/astro/AstroMath.kt:56-77) uses linear mean elements, 6 periodic terms, no eccentricity factor. `Astronomy.moonEclipticLongitude` (ios/PalmAstroKit/Sources/AstroEngine/Astronomy.swift:49-82) uses the full t^2/t^3/t^4 mean-element polynomials, 10 terms, and `e = 1 - 0.002516t - 0.0000074t^2` applied to the three M-bearing terms. Both quoted code blocks are verbatim-accurate.

I re-implemented both series in Python and swept 12,784 daily L2 datetimes (1970-01-01..2004-12-31, 09:00 local, lon 121.5E): max longitude delta 0.2142 deg, 24 element mismatches (0.188%, ~1 in 533). The auditor's two named cases reproduce to the digit — 1973-02-09: Kotlin 29.99569 (fire) vs Swift 30.07858 (earth); 1980-03-15: Kotlin 330.06304 (water) vs Swift 329.92558 (air).

I also refuted the three plausible escape hatches:
1. JD inputs are NOT the divergence source. Kotlin's integer-JDN + (hour-12)/24 - lon/15/24 and Swift's Meeus 7.1 with hourUT = localHour - lon/15 (AstroEngineImpl.swift:53-56 vs AstroEngineImpl.kt:45) agree bit-for-bit on every case I tested, including 2448057.7666666666 for 1990-06-15 14:30. CivilTime has no seconds field (Models.swift:582-590) so the seconds term Kotlin adds is always 0.
2. Sign binning is identical — `ZodiacCalculator.signAtLongitude` (line 54-58) and `Zodiac.sign(forEclipticLongitude:)` (Zodiac.swift:66-70) both do floor(lon/30) clamped to 11, so the element flip is caused solely by the longitude delta.
3. Nothing downstream absorbs it. The two `default-ruleset.json` copies are byte-identical (sha256 506f0f5d...), and ASTRO_MOON_FIRE carries careerWeight 0.5 / healthWeight 0.1 while ASTRO_MOON_WATER carries 0.1 / 0.5 — plus a different safetyTag (SAFE_GENERAL vs SAFE_HEALTH_SOFT_ONLY). So all four domain scores, the explainability rows, and the content template selected (content-templates.json:1410-1530) diverge for those users. No astro parity fixture exists to catch it: ios/shared-fixtures holds only scoring/, content/, guidance/, and ParityTests.swift never touches AstroEngine.

Severity corrected blocker -> high. It is a genuine, reproducible parity defect that violates the project's own stated standard (shared-fixtures/README.md: iOS "produce the same deterministic outputs as the Android engines (the reference implementation) for identical inputs"), but it is not launch-blocking in the crash / data-loss / safety-boundary sense: no crash, no data loss, each platform independently applies a valid safety tag for the element it derived so no soft-only guard is bypassed, and the discrepancy is only observable to the ~0.19% of L2 users who run both platforms and compare. PRD section 10 asks for "functionally equivalent" score semantics rather than bit-identical numerics, which is why I would not gate the release on it — but it should be fixed before the iOS launch, not after.

title: "1st of each month" reminder is identical to "Every 30 days", and both fire their first notification immediately on opt-in

The auditor's fix is directionally right but has two errors: `if (reminders == "monthly") 30 else 30` is a no-op, and a fixed 30-day repeat interval cannot express a calendar-monthly cadence — it drifts off the 1st within two cycles (Feb/Mar). Correct fix in SettingsViewModel.scheduleReminder, replacing lines 143-150:

For "30d" — keep periodic, add the missing initial delay:
  val request = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<ScanReminderWorker>(30, TimeUnit.DAYS)
      .setInitialDelay(30, TimeUnit.DAYS)
      .build()
  workManager.enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(WORK_NAME, ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE, request)

Note also switching REPLACE -> UPDATE (or KEEP) so re-selecting the same option does not reset the countdown.

For "monthly" — a true calendar cadence needs one-time work that reschedules itself, since no fixed period lands on the 1st:
  val next = LocalDate.now().plusMonths(1).withDayOfMonth(1).atTime(10, 0)
  val delayMin = ChronoUnit.MINUTES.between(LocalDateTime.now(), next)
  val request = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<ScanReminderWorker>()
      .setInitialDelay(delayMin, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
      .build()
  workManager.enqueueUniqueWork(WORK_NAME, ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE, request)
and at the end of ScanReminderWorker.doWork() re-enqueue the same unique work for the following month's 1st (compute from LocalDate.now() again so it self-corrects rather than drifts). Note the worker currently returns Result.success() early at line 31 when notifications are denied — the re-enqueue must happen on that path too, or the chain dies permanently the first time permission is off.

If a true calendar cadence is out of scope for launch, the honest alternative is to delete the "monthly" entry from SettingsScreen.kt:108 and both settings_reminder_monthly strings, leaving only "Every 30 days" — but the missing setInitialDelay must still be fixed either way, since that is the half that spams the user at opt-in.

title: Buttons: four corner radii, three heights, and two fixed-height buttons that clip at large font scales
evidence: ResultsScreen.kt:218 and :221 use `modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).height(48.dp)` — a FIXED height — as does DomainDetailScreen.kt:225 `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(48.dp)`; every other button in the app uses `heightIn(min = ...)`, so at a 1.5–2.0x accessibility font scale these three labels are vertically clipped inside the button. Radii and heights for the same semantic role also disagree: ResultsScreen.kt:252 `Button(... .height(56.dp), shape = RoundedCornerShape(16.dp))`; OnboardingScreen.kt:184 `Button(... .heightIn(min = 54.dp), shape = RoundedCornerShape(14.dp))`; ScanScreen.kt:251 and :277 `Button(... .heightIn(min = 54.dp))` with the default stadium shape; ScanScreen.kt:406, :423 and JournalScreen.kt:113 `heightIn(min = 48.dp)` stadium; SettingsScreen.kt:216–221 `shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)`, `heightIn(min = 48.dp)`.
fix:
Load-bearing part (the actual defect — do this): change `.height(48.dp)` to `.heightIn(min = 48.dp)` at app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/results/ResultsScreen.kt:221, ResultsScreen.kt:224, and app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/detail/DomainDetailScreen.kt:225 (note: ui/detail/, not ui/domain/ as the report said). Nothing else is required to stop the clipping — those three lines already carry `shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)`, which matches the secondary-button convention.

Consistency part (real drift, but the auditor's specific target values are an arbitrary pick — confirm the intended token with the design owner before applying): the cleanest fix is not to hand-edit seven call sites but to add the two shapes/heights as tokens in ui/theme/Theme.kt (which currently defines no `Shapes` at all, hence the M3 stadium fallback) and route buttons through them — e.g. a `PrimaryCta`/`SecondaryCta` wrapper alongside the existing OnboardingScreen.kt:182 `MainButton`, which is already exactly that pattern. Pick one primary spec (Onboarding's 14.dp / heightIn(min = 54.dp) is the most-used and a reasonable default) and apply it to ScanScreen.kt:251, :277 and ResultsScreen.kt:250; keep 12.dp / heightIn(min = 48.dp) for secondary/outlined and apply it to ScanScreen.kt:406, :423, JournalScreen.kt:113. Leave the Onboarding dropdown OutlinedButtons (56.dp) alone — they are form fields, not CTAs, and their taller height is intentional.
userImpact: Users at large system font sizes see clipped labels on "Rescan", "History" and "Add journal entry"; everyone else sees the primary button change its corner rounding between onboarding, scan, results and settings.
verifierNote: Both halves check out against the source. (1) Fixed heights: ResultsScreen.kt:221 and :224 use `Modifier.weight(1f).height(48.dp)`, DomainDetailScreen.kt:225 (in ui/detail/, not ui/domain/) uses `Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(48.dp)`. An exhaustive grep of every Button/OutlinedButton in app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui confirms these are the ONLY three that pin a height; all others use heightIn(min=…). (2) The clip is real, not theoretical: M3 Button applies ButtonDefaults.ContentPadding (8.dp vertical) inside the fixed 48.dp box, leaving 32.dp for the label; Theme.kt:127 states buttons deliberately stay on stock labelLarge (14sp/20sp lineHeight), so at fontScale ~1.6-2.0 the line box exceeds 32.dp and Compose Text (default TextOverflow.Clip) clips its draw when hasVisualOverflow. I checked for an escape hatch and found none — there is no Density/fontScale override anywhere in app/src/main/kotlin, and ScoreGauge.kt:68 explicitly adapts to LocalDensity.fontScale, so the codebase's own convention is to respect scaling. Affected labels are results_rescan (重新掃描), results_history (歷史記錄) and detail_journal_button. (3) Radii drift is factual, not just taste: Theme.kt declares no custom Shapes, so unshaped buttons fall back to the M3 stadium; the same primary-CTA role therefore renders at 14.dp (Onboarding:183), stadium (Scan:251,:277,:406,:423; Journal:113), 16.dp (Results:250) and 12.dp (Settings:216). Only defects found in the report are cosmetic: three line numbers cited 2-3 lines early (218/221/252 vs actual 221/224/250) and the wrong subdirectory for DomainDetailScreen.

title: The comparability score is computed, stored and composed into the payload but never shown anywhere in the UI
evidence: PRD §3.3, the product's stated differentiator, reads: "Delta is shown with a comparability score." The value exists end to end — DeltaEngineImpl.kt:26 `val comparabilityScore = computeComparability(prev, current)`, persisted at Entities.kt:61, rehydrated at ResultRepository.kt:64, and placed on every payload by ContentComposerImpl (`comparabilityScore = input.deltaResult?.comparabilityScore`). Its only consumer is the boolean gate at ResultsViewModel.kt:131, `val deltaComparable = delta != null && delta.comparabilityBucket != ComparabilityBucket.LOW`; the numeric score is discarded. `grep -rn "comparab" app/src` returns zero hits in any Compose screen and zero string resources — nothing in ResultsScreen.kt, DomainDetailScreen.kt, ExplainabilityScreen.kt or HistoryScreen.kt renders it, so a user who sees "▲+8" is given no basis for judging how comparable the two scans were.
fix:
1) ResultsViewModel: add `val comparabilityScore: Int? = null` and `val deltaApproximate: Boolean = false` to ResultsState (ResultsViewModel.kt:42-56). In buildDomainCards the delta is already fetched (line 125-131); hoist it so load() can set both — `comparabilityScore = delta?.takeIf { it.comparabilityBucket != ComparabilityBucket.LOW }?.comparabilityScore` and `deltaApproximate = delta?.comparabilityBucket == ComparabilityBucket.MED`.

2) Placement — the auditor's "under the delta row in HeroMetaRow" is wrong: HeroMetaRow (ResultsScreen.kt:316-339) has no delta row; deltas render per-domain-card via DeltaIndicator at line 469. Comparability is a single per-month value, so render it as a sibling chip next to the existing scan-quality chip in HeroMetaRow, matching that chip's Surface/Icon/Text treatment. Render it only when comparabilityScore != null, so the first-ever scan (delta == null) shows nothing rather than an empty or zero value.

3) Strings must be added to BOTH app/src/main/res/values/strings_results.xml and app/src/main/res/values-zh-rTW/strings_results.xml — zh-Hant is the launch locale, and an English-only string would ship untranslated to the primary market. Follow the existing results_scan_quality_chip pattern ("Scan quality %1$d/100" / "掃描品質 %1$d/100"), e.g. results_comparability_chip = "Comparable to last month %1$d/100" / "與上月可比度 %1$d/100". values-hi/strings.xml carries no results strings, so it is out of scope.

4) MED weakening (PRD line 89): when deltaApproximate is true, tint the DeltaIndicator glyph with extended.deltaNeutral instead of deltaPositive/deltaNegative and append an "approximate" qualifier — and update the TalkBack contentDescription at ResultsScreen.kt:483-492 to match, otherwise the visual weakening is invisible to screen readers.

5) Adjacent gap the proposed fix misses: HistoryViewModel.kt:57-63 recomputes deltas from raw month-to-month score differences and never consults DeltaResult, so a LOW-comparability delta that Results blocks is still rendered by HistoryScreen.DeltaText (HistoryScreen.kt:151,165-171). Route History's deltas through ResultRepository.getDeltaFor with the same gate, or file it as a separate finding.

6) Tests: ResultsViewModelTest already covers the HIGH (line 111) and LOW (line 125) buckets; add a MED case asserting the delta is still shown, deltaApproximate is true, and comparabilityScore is exposed.
userImpact: Month-over-month arrows are presented as bare facts. The user cannot tell whether a +8 came from two clean, comparable scans or from two scans with very different lighting and palm coverage — the honesty the delta feature was specced to provide.
verifierNote: Every cited line checks out. DeltaEngineImpl.kt:26 computes comparabilityScore, Entities.kt:61 persists it, ResultRepository.kt:56/64 rehydrates it, ContentComposerImpl.kt:109 puts it on every SemanticPayload.scoreCard — and the only consumer in app code is the boolean gate at ResultsViewModel.kt:131. The numeric value never reaches ResultsState (lines 42-56) or DomainCard (20-31). `grep -rni "comparab" app/src` returns hits only in ResultsViewModel.kt and two test files: zero in ResultsScreen.kt, DomainDetailScreen.kt, ExplainabilityScreen.kt, HistoryScreen.kt, and zero string resources in values/ or values-zh-rTW/. I could not find it surfaced anywhere else, including iOS (ios/App has no comparability reference; only PalmAstroKit engine + fixtures). PRD line 88 ("Delta is shown with a comparability score") and line 89 ("Low-comparability deltas are weakened or blocked") are therefore half-implemented: LOW is blocked by the gate, but MED renders identically to HIGH via DeltaIndicator (ResultsScreen.kt:534-543), and the score itself is never shown. Not a style preference — a specified, computed, stored value that no surface renders. Severity stays medium rather than high: computeComparability hardcodes handMatch/calcLevel/timeGap to 100, giving a floor of 45 and typical values of 85-100, so LOW (<50, requires ~50-point quality delta AND ~0.3 coverage delta) and MED are rare in practice; the transparency gap is real but rarely produces a materially misleading arrow.

title: 139 KB content-templates.json is read and deserialized on the main thread while the start-destination screen composes
evidence: `ResultsViewModel` takes `private val guidanceBuilder: GuidanceBuilder = GuidanceBuilder(),` as a constructor parameter. Hilt satisfies it from `EngineModule.kt:51` — `@Provides @Singleton fun provideGuidanceBuilder(): GuidanceBuilder = GuidanceBuilder()` — and `GuidanceBuilder`'s default argument (GuidanceBuilder.kt:54) is `ContentTemplates.default()`, which resolves `ContentTemplates.kt:171` `private val defaultTemplates: ContentTemplates by lazy { fromResource() }` → line 178 `ContentTemplates::class.java.getResourceAsStream("/content-templates.json")?.bufferedReader()?.readText()` followed by `Json.decodeFromString`. The built artifact confirms the payload size: `base/root/content-templates.json` is 138,963 bytes in `app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab`. The whole chain runs when Dagger constructs `ResultsViewModel`, which happens in `ResultsScreen.kt:68` (`viewModel: ResultsViewModel = hiltViewModel()`) during composition on the main thread — and Results is the start destination for every returning user (`AppNavigation.kt:43`, `val startRoute = if (hasProfile) "results" else Route.Onboarding.path`).
fix:
The auditor's fix is directionally right but wrong in two concrete ways.

(1) Dropping the default value breaks the build. ResultsViewModelTest.kt:86 calls `ResultsViewModel(handle, resultRepository, userRepository, featureFlags)` with no builder argument. If line 65 becomes a non-defaulted `dagger.Lazy<GuidanceBuilder>`, that call site fails to compile and the two mockk call sites at lines 190 and 206 must wrap their builder as `dagger.Lazy { builder }`. Either update all three test call sites, or keep a default of `dagger.Lazy { GuidanceBuilder() }`.

(2) `dagger.Lazy.get()` alone does NOT move the parse off the main thread. Line 161 runs inside `buildGuidanceSummary`, called from the `viewModelScope.launch` block in `load()`, and viewModelScope dispatches on `Dispatchers.Main.immediate`. Deferring the `.get()` into that coroutine only moves the parse from constructor time to just after the first DB suspension — still on the main thread, still blocking a frame. Worse, if the proposed PalmAstroApp warm-up is in flight, the main thread blocks on the SYNCHRONIZED `by lazy` monitor in ContentTemplates.kt:171 waiting for the IO thread.

Corrected fix:
- ResultsViewModel.kt:65 -> `private val guidanceBuilder: dagger.Lazy<GuidanceBuilder> = dagger.Lazy { GuidanceBuilder() },` (keeps test call sites at lines 86/190/206 compiling with a small wrap at 190/206).
- Make the guidance build genuinely off-main rather than relying on a race: change `buildGuidanceSummary` to a `suspend fun` and wrap its body in `withContext(Dispatchers.Default) { ... }`, calling `guidanceBuilder.get().build(payloads, grade, language)` inside. The call site in `load()` is already inside a coroutine, so no other change is needed. Apply the same `withContext(Dispatchers.Default)` around the `guidanceBuilder.build(...)` call at GuidanceViewModel.kt:66 and the same `dagger.Lazy` change at GuidanceViewModel.kt:42 (GuidanceViewModel has no default arg and no test constructing it without the builder beyond the mockk at GuidanceViewModelTest.kt:31, which needs the same wrap).
- The PalmAstroApp.kt:53-56 warm-up is still worth adding as belt-and-braces (`runCatching { com.palmastro.content.ContentTemplates.default() }` inside the existing appScope.launch, before the installId call), but it is an optimization, not the fix — with the withContext in place, correctness no longer depends on it winning the race.
userImpact: The first composition of the home screen stalls the UI thread reading and JSON-parsing 139 KB out of the APK. On a cold start the user watches a blank screen for an extra ~100-300 ms before their monthly result appears.
verifierNote: The chain is real and I could not refute it. ResultsViewModel.kt:65 takes GuidanceBuilder; Hilt satisfies it from EngineModule.kt:51 (@Provides @Singleton GuidanceBuilder()), whose default arg GuidanceBuilder.kt:54 = ContentTemplates.default() resolves the SYNCHRONIZED `by lazy` at ContentTemplates.kt:171, which does getResourceAsStream + readText + Json.decodeFromString on a 138,963-byte resource (verified: engine-content/src/main/resources/content-templates.json). Dagger's DoubleCheck creates that singleton at ViewModel construction, which happens synchronously inside composition via hiltViewModel() at ResultsScreen.kt:68, and Results is the start destination for returning users (AppNavigation.kt:43). I checked every plausible refutation: nothing warms the lazy earlier (PalmAstroApp.kt and MainActivity.kt never reference ContentTemplates; the other consumers ContentComposerImpl and SafetyFilterImpl are @Singleton and only requested on the scan path), and the Kotlin default value is dead on the Hilt path so it does not avoid the parse. What the auditor got wrong is the magnitude: I benchmarked the real compiled engine-content-0.1.0.jar on JDK 17 and the cold first parse, including serializer class loading, is 35.6 ms with JIT and 60.2 ms fully interpreted (-Xint, a pessimistic stand-in for cold ART); warm reparse is 2 ms / 29 ms. So the stall is tens of milliseconds, not the claimed 100-300 ms, it lands inside a window where MainActivity is already showing a blank Box awaiting userRepository.exists(), and it is nowhere near ANR territory. That is a genuine main-thread I/O + parse defect worth fixing, but medium, not high.

title: Picking only a birth place silently records a fabricated 12:00 birth time and upgrades the reading to L2
evidence: BirthDetailsStep pre-seeds `var selHour by remember { mutableStateOf(12) }` / `var selMinute by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }` (lines 426-427) and the confirm button passes them unconditionally: `MainButton(stringResource(R.string.ob_birth_details_confirm)) { onContinue(selHour, selMinute, selectedLocation) }` (line 474). The callback at line 141 then calls `viewModel.setBirthTime(h, m)` always, and OnboardingViewModel.kt:73 is `fun setBirthTime(hour: Int, minute: Int) = _state.update { it.copy(hasBirthTime = true, ...) }`. So a user who searches a city, taps it, and presses confirm without ever opening the hour/minute dropdowns gets `hasBirthTime = true` + `hasBirthPlace = true`, and OnboardingViewModel.kt:97 `val calcLevel = if (s.hasBirthTime && s.hasBirthPlace) "L2" else "L1"` marks the profile L2. The summary then displays `ob_summary_l2` = "L2 (detailed)" (strings_onboarding.xml:107), and AstroEngineImpl.kt:47-55 computes the Moon sign and the Ascendant from that invented noon — the ascendant advances a full sign roughly every two hours. The birth-place field has an explicit `ob_birth_place_unknown` escape (line 468); the time field has none.
fix: Make the time as genuinely opt-in as the place already is, rather than tracking a separate boolean. In BirthDetailsStep (OnboardingScreen.kt:426-427) change the state to nullable — `var selHour by remember { mutableStateOf<Int?>(null) }` and `var selMinute by remember { mutableStateOf<Int?>(null) }` — mirroring `selectedLocation`. CRITICAL and missing from the original proposal: the button labels at lines 442 and 450 must reflect the unset state (e.g. `selHour?.toString()?.padStart(2,'0') ?: "--"`), otherwise the field still reads "Hour: 12" and the misleading display survives the fix. Widen the callback to `onContinue: (Int?, Int?, Location?)` and pass `selHour, selMinute` straight through; at line 474 treat a chosen hour with untouched minute as minute 0 (`selMinute ?: 0`). At OnboardingScreen.kt:141 call `viewModel.setBirthTime(h, m)` only when `h != null` — OnboardingViewModel needs no change, since hasBirthTime already defaults false and line 103 already nulls birthTimeMinutes when it is false. Add an "unknown birth time" DropdownMenuItem at the top of the hour menu (line 445) that sets `selHour = null; selMinute = null`, mirroring line 468; the new string must be added to BOTH app/src/main/res/values/strings_onboarding.xml and app/src/main/res/values-zh-rTW/strings_onboarding.xml, since zh-Hant is the launch language and a missing translation would surface English text in the primary market. Recommended alongside: add birth-time and birth-place rows to SummaryStep (OnboardingScreen.kt:515-569) so the L2 claim shows the data it rests on, since onboarding is the only writer of birth time in the app and there is no later surface to correct a wrong value. Existing OnboardingViewModelTest cases at lines 175 and 197 exercise the ViewModel directly and are unaffected.
userImpact: The app tells the user their reading is "L2 (detailed)" and derives Moon and Ascendant signals from a birth time they never entered. Any user who supplies a city but not a time gets a more-precise-looking reading built on invented data — a transparency failure in the one place the product claims extra accuracy.
verifierNote: Every link verified. BirthDetailsStep (OnboardingScreen.kt:426-427) seeds selHour=12/selMinute=0 with no null state, and confirm (line 474) passes them unconditionally; the callback at line 141 always calls viewModel.setBirthTime(h, m), which sets hasBirthTime=true (OnboardingViewModel.kt:73). With a city picked, OnboardingViewModel.kt:97 stamps calcLevel="L2". ScanViewModel.kt:400-406 rebuilds LocalTime.of(12,0) from the profile and AstroEngineImpl.kt:33/44-53 derives ASTRO_MOON_* and ASTRO_ASC_* from that invented instant — the ascendant shifts a sign roughly every two hours, so it is effectively arbitrary. Three refutations tried and failed: (1) "the 12 is visible" — it is rendered at line 442, but styled identically to a chosen value, and SummaryStep (515-569) shows only "Analysis: L2 (detailed)" and never prints the birth time or place, so the confirmation surface asserts precision without showing its input; (2) "Skip covers it" — skipBirthDetails() (line 75) clears hasBirthTime AND hasBirthPlace together, so "city known, time unknown" is unrepresentable, while the place field alone has the ob_birth_place_unknown escape at line 468; (3) "guarded downstream" — nothing guards it, and grep for setBirthTime/birthTimeMinutes shows onboarding is the only writer in the app, with no settings surface to correct it, so the fabricated noon is permanent. Severity medium is correct: confined to place-without-time users, L1 sun signals unaffected, no crash or data loss, but it mislabels precision and invents inputs exactly where the product claims extra accuracy.

title: First scan is blocked by a 7.8 MB undisclosed model download shown as an indeterminate spinner with no progress and no cancel
evidence: `private const val MODEL_URL = "https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/.../hand_landmarker.task"` and the pinned checksum comment states "(7,819,105 bytes)". `app/src/main/assets/models/` is EMPTY, so `hasAssetModel()` (ModelManager.kt:107-112) always returns false and every fresh install must fetch 7.8 MB before angle 1. ScanScreen.kt:150 routes that to `ModelDownloadingScreen()` (ScanScreen.kt:382-388), which is `CircularProgressIndicator()` + `Text(stringResource(R.string.scan_downloading))` = "Downloading analysis model…" (strings.xml:44) — indeterminate, no byte count, no percentage, no cancel. Nothing in onboarding mentions a download: ob_camera_body and ob_camera_point_local (strings_onboarding.xml:114-115) say only that photos are "processed on your device".
fix:
1) Progress (the substantive part): give ModelManager.downloadModel an onProgress: (Long, Long) -> Unit and replace input.copyTo(output) in attemptDownload (ModelManager.kt:163-167) with a manual read loop that emits bytes read; take the total from conn.contentLengthLong. Surface downloadedBytes/totalBytes on ScanState and have ModelDownloadingScreen use a determinate LinearProgressIndicator(progress = { downloaded / total }) — but keep the indeterminate form as the fallback when contentLengthLong <= 0, since the header can be absent, and reset the counter per retry attempt so downloadWithRetry's 3 attempts do not make the bar jump backwards.

2) Exit, not disclosure, is the other real gap: add an onExit ("Not now") affordance to both ModelDownloadingScreen and the MODEL_DOWNLOAD_FAILED/MODEL_CORRUPT ErrorScreen, since AppNavigation pops Onboarding inclusive and system back therefore kills the app on first run. Cancel should also flip modelDownloading off and leave the .tmp/.lock cleanup to attemptDownload's finally block; note the blocking stream read will not honor coroutine cancellation mid-transfer, so treat "Not now" as leave-the-screen rather than abort-the-socket unless you also close the connection.

3) Drop the "disclose it" step as written — the privacy policy already discloses the download at privacy_policy_en.html:23/:49 and its zh-TW twin. If you still want it in onboarding, the useful version is a size/one-time hint on the camera step, and it MUST ship in values-zh-rTW/strings_onboarding.xml as well as values/, because zh-Hant is the launch locale; the proposed English-only string would ship untranslated to the primary market.
userImpact: On a slow or metered connection the user stares at a spinner that could last minutes with zero indication of progress or size, having been told the app works on-device. Offline, they hit an error screen whose only button is Retry, with no way back into the app.
verifierNote:
Verified against source. app/src/main/assets/models/ is empty and not gitignored, and no Gradle/script step populates it, so ModelManager.hasAssetModel() (ModelManager.kt:106-112) is always false on a fresh install and ScanViewModel.checkAndDownloadModel() (ScanViewModel.kt:136-159) always hits the network before the first capture. attemptDownload uses input.copyTo(output) (ModelManager.kt:163-167) with no progress hook anywhere in the call chain, and ScanScreen.kt:150 routes modelDownloading to ModelDownloadingScreen (ScanScreen.kt:382-388), which is a bare CircularProgressIndicator plus R.string.scan_downloading — indeterminate, no bytes, no percent, no cancel. ErrorScreen (ScanScreen.kt:394-410) renders exactly one Button wired to retryModelDownload(), and AppNavigation.kt:58-64 navigates onboarding->Scan with popUpTo(Onboarding){inclusive=true}, so on first run the back stack is empty and system back exits the app: the offline dead end is real. CameraEducationStep (OnboardingScreen.kt:588-599) does show only ob_camera_point_local and ob_camera_point_denied.

Two parts of the finding are wrong, which is why I lowered severity. (1) "Undisclosed" is false: app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy_en.html:23 and :49 (and the zh-TW file at the same lines) disclose the download explicitly — "connects to the internet once, to download the hand-detection model file", naming storage.googleapis.com, one-time, integrity-checked; sc_err_download_why also says "one-time download". The onboarding copy is not contradicted either: ob_camera_point_local claims only that *photos* are processed on device, which a model fetch does not violate. (2) The download is not fully serialized in front of the user: ScanViewModel.init fires it at ScanScreen composition, so it runs behind ExplainerScreen, TipsScreen, and the camera permission dialog; the spinner covers only the residual time. What survives is a genuine first-run UX defect — an indeterminate, uncancellable wait plus a hard dead end when offline — which is medium, not high.

title: iOS has no History surface — the data is loaded and then never shown
evidence: MainTabView (PalmAstroApp.swift:36-58) has exactly three tabs: `ResultsView` (tab_results), `JournalView` (tab_journal), `SettingsView` (tab_settings). Android ships a dedicated history screen at app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/history/HistoryScreen.kt with its own strings — app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:90-92 `history_title` = "History", `history_single_record` = "Only one record — scan more months to see trends", `history_score_desc`. iOS loads the data and drops it: AppModel.swift:38 `@Published private(set) var history: [MonthlyResult] = []`, populated at AppModel.swift:82 and :196 with `resultRepository.listHistory(limit: 24)`, but the only consumer is the month-over-month delta lookup at AppModel.swift:147. `grep -n "history" ios/App/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable.strings` returns nothing — there are no history strings on iOS at all. No iOS view file references `model.history`.
fix: Mirror Android's information architecture rather than adding a fourth tab (Android reaches History from a button on the Results screen, ResultsScreen.kt:224; a 4th tab also cuts against PRD §9's "native, not a direct Android port" HIG direction). Concretely: (a) add ios/App/History/HistoryView.swift rendering model.history (already populated 24 deep at AppModel.swift:82/196, newest first per Repositories.swift:5) as a List of month cards — monthKey, grade chip, the four domain rows with score bar and signed delta, and the confidence line; (b) push it from ResultsView via a toolbar/list entry inside the existing NavigationStack in PalmAstroApp.swift:38-43, leaving the tab bar at three. Compute the per-domain deltas in the view the way HistoryViewModel.kt does — element i vs element i+1 of the chronologically-DESC list — rather than reading semanticPayloads[...].scoreCard.delta, because that stored delta was computed once at scan time against whatever record was previous then and will not stay consistent across the list. Tap-through to a past month additionally requires ResultsView to accept a monthKey instead of unconditionally reading model.latestResult (Android does this via results?monthKey=, AppNavigation.kt:150); if that refactor is out of scope, ship the list read-only and skip the tap-through. Strings to add to BOTH ios/App/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable.strings and zh-Hant.lproj/Localizable.strings, using the Android copy: history_title, history_single_record (values/strings.xml:90-91, values-zh-rTW/strings.xml:103), and history_empty_title, history_empty_desc, history_delta_desc (values/strings_results.xml:22-24, values-zh-rTW/strings_results.xml:24) — the auditor's list is wrong here: it names history_score_desc, which HistoryScreen.kt never uses (it is a dead string on Android), and omits the three empty-state/delta keys the screen actually needs. No tab_history string is needed under this placement.
userImpact: An iOS user who has scanned for several months can never see their trend — the core month-over-month reflection loop the product is built around exists only on Android, even though iOS is already storing and reading 24 months of results.
verifierNote: Verified on both platforms. iOS MainTabView (ios/App/PalmAstroApp.swift:32-60) has exactly three tabs (Results/Journal/Settings); no view under ios/App references model.history; ios/App/Resources/en.lproj/Localizable.strings and zh-Hant.lproj contain no history_* or tab_history keys; ResultsView renders only model.latestResult, so no past month can be opened. Android ships app/src/main/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/ui/history/HistoryScreen.kt, routed at navigation/AppNavigation.kt:147, entered from ResultsScreen.kt:224 (onHistoryClick -> AppNavigation.kt:79), with a "history" deep link at navigation/DeepLinkHandler.kt:37. So the surface genuinely exists on Android and is absent on iOS. Two corrections to the auditor. (1) The title "loaded and then never shown" is inaccurate: AppModel.swift:147 feeds history into deltaEngine.computeDelta and that delta is displayed as the arrow + magnitude in DomainCard (ResultsView.swift:134-143), so month-over-month change IS visible per domain; what is missing is browsing/opening prior months, not the trend signal entirely. (2) PRD §54 lists "User can view history" as P1, not P0; it is not in the §9 iOS Launch Gates nor the §10 parity list. Severity medium still stands (a whole launch-criterion screen is missing on a shipping platform), but the "core loop exists only on Android" framing is overstated.

title: Dark theme: journal delete icon is 2.68:1 against its own card
evidence: L137 `colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant),` and L154-158 `Icon(Icons.Outlined.Delete, contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.journal_delete), tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error,)`. title: An unsaved journal entry is discarded silently on back — no autosave, no unsaved-changes prompt
evidence: The app bar's `navigationIcon` calls `onBack` unconditionally (lines 37-41), which is `navController.popBackStack()` (AppNavigation.kt:160). `JournalViewModel` holds the draft only in `MutableStateFlow(JournalState())` (line 28) with no `SavedStateHandle` write and no autosave — `save()` runs only on the explicit button (line 63). `Button(enabled = state.text.isNotBlank() && !state.isSaved)` (JournalScreen.kt:114) proves the screen already knows when a draft is unsaved, but nothing acts on it. There is no `BackHandler` anywhere in app/src/main. Up to 500 characters (`JournalRepository.MAX_CHARS`) of reflective writing vanish on back, on system back, and on process death.
fix:
Track dirtiness against the persisted text rather than reusing the button's enabled condition.

1. JournalViewModel.kt — add `val savedText: String = ""` to JournalState. In `load()`, set `savedText = existing?.text ?: ""` alongside `text`. In `save()`, set `savedText = _state.value.text` in the same `copy` that sets `isSaved = true` (do this before the trailing `load()` call so a slow re-read cannot flash a dirty state). Expose `val isDirty get() = text != savedText` on JournalState, or compute it in the screen. Note JournalRepository.saveEntry trims and truncates (`text.take(MAX_CHARS).trim()`), so seed `savedText` from what the repository actually stored — re-read it in `load()` as is already done — otherwise trailing whitespace makes an entry permanently "dirty".

2. JournalScreen.kt — `val hasUnsaved = state.isDirty && state.text.isNotBlank()`; `var confirmDiscard by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }`; `BackHandler(enabled = hasUnsaved) { confirmDiscard = true }` (import androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler); change navigationIcon to `IconButton(onClick = { if (hasUnsaved) confirmDiscard = true else onBack() })`. Render `if (confirmDiscard) AlertDialog(onDismissRequest = { confirmDiscard = false }, ...)` with confirmButton "Save" -> `{ viewModel.save(); confirmDiscard = false; onBack() }` and dismissButton "Discard" -> `{ confirmDiscard = false; onBack() }`. Give the dialog a third exit (or rely on onDismissRequest) so the user can return to editing rather than being forced to choose save-or-lose.

3. Also fix the Button's `enabled` (line 114) to use the same `hasUnsaved`, so a freshly loaded, unmodified entry does not present an enabled Save that writes an identical row.

4. Add `journal_discard_title`, `journal_discard_message`, `journal_discard_confirm`, `journal_discard_dismiss` to BOTH app/src/main/res/values/strings_detail.xml and app/src/main/res/values-zh-rTW/strings_detail.xml — zh-Hant is the launch language, so a missing translation there ships as English to the primary market.

5. Optional, closes the process-death half of the finding: make the draft survive by hoisting it into SavedStateHandle — `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow("draft", "")` written from `updateText` — since a BackHandler does nothing for a process kill.
userImpact: The user writes a personal reflection, taps back out of habit, and it is gone with no warning — in the one surface of the app that exists purely to hold their own words.

JournalViewModel.kt:28 — draft lives only in `MutableStateFlow(JournalState())`; SavedStateHandle is read for `monthKey`/`domain` (lines 31-32) but never written, so nothing survives process death. `save()` (line 63) is reachable only from the Button at JournalScreen.kt:111-115. `grep -rn "BackHandler" app/src --include="*.kt"` returns zero hits, so system back and predictive back also drop the draft with no warning. JournalRepository.kt:15 confirms MAX_CHARS = 500. OutlinedTextField(

    onValueChange = { viewModel.updateText(it) },
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxWidth()
        .heightIn(min = 200.dp),
    label = { Text(stringResource(R.string.journal_prompt)) },

title: The monthly rescan loop — the product's core retention mechanic — has no stale-month prompt anywhere
evidence: `resultRepository.getRecent(1).firstOrNull()` loads the most recent reading regardless of age, and `ResultsState` (lines 42-56) carries no staleness field. `YearMonth.now()` appears nowhere in the UI layer (grep across app/src/main/kotlin returns only ScanViewModel.kt:195 and :416). The only rescan entry point is `OutlinedButton(onClick = onScanClick, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).height(48.dp))` at ResultsScreen.kt:218 — a low-emphasis button in a LazyColumn item that sits below the hero, the guidance card and all four domain cards, i.e. off-screen at first paint.

AppNavigation.kt:150 routes History taps to "results?monthKey=$monthKey" and DeepLinkHandler.kt:51 builds the same route; ResultsViewModel:70,77-78 serves those through targetMonthKey. Setting isStale = entity.monthKey != YearMonth.now().toString() unconditionally would show "A new month has begun — scan again" on top of every deliberately opened historical reading. (2) ResultsScreen.ResultsList (line 188) — when state.isStale, emit a Card as the first item, above HeroCard, with a filled Button(onClick = onScanClick) using the existing R.string.results_rescan; do not attach entranceReveal to it (freshArrival implies a scan just completed for the current month, so play && isStale cannot co-occur) and leave the existing reveal indices untouched. (3) Feed the body the formatted month, not the raw key: reuse rememberHeroMonthTitle(state.monthKey) for the %1$s argument — "2026-08" reads badly in zh-Hant. (4) Add results_new_month_title / results_new_month_desc to app/src/main/res/values/strings_results.xml AND app/src/main/res/values-zh-rTW/strings_results.xml with authored Traditional Chinese copy (zh-Hant is the launch language; no English fallback). title: Birthday and birth-time/place pickers use `remember`, so a rotation mid-onboarding silently resets them to defaults
evidence: `var selMonth by remember { mutableStateOf(existing?.monthValue ?: 6) }` / `selDay ?: 15` / `selYear ?: 1990` (lines 308-310), and in BirthDetailsStep `var selHour by remember { mutableStateOf(12) }`, `selMinute`, `var selectedLocation by remember { mutableStateOf<Location?>(null) }`, `var searchQuery by remember { mutableStateOf("") }` (lines 426-431). These values reach the ViewModel only when the user presses Next (lines 137, 141), and `remember` does not survive Activity recreation. AndroidManifest.xml declares neither `android:screenOrientation` nor `android:configChanges` on MainActivity, so every rotation recreates it. `OnboardingViewModel` compounds this: `private val _state = MutableStateFlow(OnboardingState())` (line 56) with no SavedStateHandle, so process death restarts all 10 steps from zero.
fix: In OnboardingScreen.kt, add `import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable` and switch only the user-input state to it — `selMonth`, `selDay`, `selYear` (308-310), `selHour`, `selMinute` (426-427), and `searchQuery` (431). Leave `monthExpanded`/`dayExpanded`/`yearExpanded`/`hourExpanded`/`minuteExpanded`/`locExpanded` as plain `remember`: saving them would re-open a dropdown after rotation, which is wrong. Do NOT wrap `selectedLocation` (430) directly — `Location` (line 49) is a plain private data class, neither Parcelable nor Serializable, so `rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<Location?>(null) }` throws IllegalArgumentException the moment a non-null value is saved. Store the name instead: `var selectedLocationName by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }` and derive `val selectedLocation = remember(selectedLocationName) { locations.firstOrNull { it.name == selectedLocationName } }`. Also fix the same root cause on the back-navigation path, which is worse and needs no rotation: BirthDetailsStep (line 425) takes no `existing` parameter, unlike BirthdayStep(state.birthday) at 137. Navigating Back from TONE to BIRTH_DETAILS re-renders 12:00 and a blank place even though the ViewModel holds the user's real values, and re-pressing Confirm calls `setBirthTime(12, 0)` while `setBirthPlace` is skipped because `loc == null` — leaving `hasBirthPlace = true` with stale coordinates and a silently wiped birth time. Pass the existing values in (e.g. `BirthDetailsStep(existingHour = state.birthTimeHour.takeIf { state.hasBirthTime }, existingMinute = ..., existingPlaceName = state.birthPlaceName.takeIf { state.hasBirthPlace }, ...)`) and seed the rememberSaveable initial values from them. Treat the OnboardingViewModel SavedStateHandle mirroring as a separate lower-priority item — the rememberSaveable change alone already survives rotation, and process death mid-onboarding is far rarer.
userImpact: A user who rotates their phone while hunting for their birth time on a certificate returns to find the date silently reset to 15 June 1990 — and may not notice, submitting a wrong birthday that invalidates every astrology signal in every future reading.

title: An over-exposed frame is coached with "move somewhere brighter"; the correct string is unreachable
evidence: findWorstComponent maps the exposure channel to a single one-directional reason: `"low_light" to scores.exposure,` (line 45). But the exposure metric is symmetric around mid-grey — ImageQualityAnalyzer.kt:80 computes `val exposure = (1.0f - abs(mean - 127f) / 127f).coerceIn(0.0f, 1.0f)` — so a blown-out frame (mean ~220) and a dark frame (mean ~35) both produce a low score and both emit `"low_light"`. ScanScreen.kt:86 maps that to `R.string.coach_low_light` = "Not enough light — move somewhere brighter" (strings_scan.xml:25). The correct copy already ships and is unreachable: strings_scan.xml:26 `<string name="coach_over_exposure">Too bright — move away from the light</string>`, wired at ScanScreen.kt:87 and keyed in CoachingHints.keys as `"over_exposure"`, a reason nothing ever produces. PRD §13.2 requires "Quality gate explains failure reason."
fix:
The auditor's fix is sound and I verified it compiles logically; two refinements. (1) In ImageQualityAnalyzer.kt add `val meanBrightness: Float = 127f` to ImageQualityMetrics — place it after `stability` (any position works since line 85 passes the first four positionally and the rest by name, and ScanViewModelTest.kt:465 uses named args) — and populate it at line 85 from the `mean` already computed at line 79. (2) In ScanViewModel.onFrameCaptured replace line 242 with:
  var reason = gateResult.failReason ?: "hand_not_detected"
  if (reason == "low_light" && metrics.meanBrightness > 127f) reason = "over_exposure"
`metrics` is in scope there and the rewrite lands before the analytics.emit at line 243, so the scan_angle_quality_fail reason dimension is corrected too — worth keeping in that order. CoachingHints.keyFor("over_exposure") and the ScanScreen.kt:87 branch already exist, so no engine-contract or string changes are needed. Refinement: use a small deadband (e.g. `> 140f`) rather than a bare `> 127f`, since at mean 128 the exposure score is ~0.99 and could never be the worst component anyway — the deadband just documents intent and avoids flip-flopping copy on near-neutral frames. Add a ScanViewModelTest case feeding ImageQualityMetrics(meanBrightness = 205f, exposure = 0.40f, blur = 0.45f, glare = 0.55f, coverage = 0.60f) and asserting coachingHintKey == "coach_over_exposure". Apply the mirror change in ios/PalmAstroKit/Sources/ScanQualityEngine (its QualityGateImpl.swift:62 has the same one-directional map) or the parity fixtures will diverge; note iOS CoachingHints.swift:14 maps under_exposure to "coach_under_exposure" while Android maps it to "coach_low_light", so confirm the iOS string catalog actually has coach_under_exposure while you are in that file.
userImpact: A user scanning under a bright lamp or in direct sun is told to find more light. Following the coaching makes the next capture worse, and the quality gate keeps rejecting the angle with no way to progress — the retry loop the scan acceptance criteria exist to prevent.
verifierNote: Every claimed link verified in source. QualityGateImpl.kt:45 maps the exposure channel only to "low_light"; ImageQualityAnalyzer.kt:80 computes exposure as `1 - abs(mean-127)/127`, symmetric around mid-grey, and discards `mean` (ImageQualityMetrics, lines 20-28, has no brightness field), so a bright frame and a dark frame emit the identical reason. ScanViewModel.kt:242 forwards it verbatim to CoachingHints.keyFor, and ScanScreen.kt:86 resolves it to coach_low_light ("Not enough light — move somewhere brighter"). A repo-wide grep excluding build dirs confirms NOTHING anywhere produces the literal "over_exposure": the shipped strings (values/strings_scan.xml:26 and values-zh-rTW/strings_scan.xml:26), the CoachingHints key entry, and the ScanScreen.kt:87 branch are all dead code. iOS has the identical one-directional map at ios/PalmAstroKit/Sources/ScanQualityEngine/QualityGateImpl.swift:62, so it is a cross-platform defect, not an Android-only slip. I tried to refute on reachability and could not: stability is hard-coded 0.9, so a gate fail needs blur+glare+exposure+coverage < 2.1; for exposure to be the strict minimum the other three exceed it, giving 3e < 2.1-e, i.e. e < 0.525, i.e. mean > 193 — genuinely over-exposed and satisfiable (e.g. mean 203, blur 0.45, glare 0.55, coverage 0.60 -> composite 58, worst = exposure, copy says "move somewhere brighter"). Warm indoor light widens the window because the glare channel needs r,g,b all >240 and tungsten depresses blue. Two auditor overstatements, which is why I hold severity at medium rather than raising it: in extreme blow-out (mean ~240) the glare channel usually hits 0 first and wins minByOrNull, producing the sensible "Avoid direct light sources", so the inverted copy occurs in a mid-band rather than for every bright frame; and the "no way to progress" claim is too strong, since improving blur/coverage can still clear the composite gate. title: Both reminder options schedule the same 30-day job with no initial delay, so the reminder fires the moment it is enabled

title: Scan photos can survive up to 30 hours despite the "within 24 hours" promise in the policy and the Play declaration

The worker deletes only files older than `const val RETENTION_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000L` (ScanImageCleanupWorker.kt:74) via `if (file.lastModified() < cutoff) file.deleteRecursively()` (line 61). A file that turns 24 hours old one minute after a cleanup run is not deleted until the next run, up to 6 hours later — a worst case of ~30 hours, before any additional Doze deferral WorkManager applies. app/src/main/assets/legal/privacy_policy_en.html:65 states `deleted automatically within 24 hours of capture by default`, line 24 repeats `automatically deleted within 24 hours`, and docs/store/play/permissions.md:20-21 gives Play the console text "auto-deleted within 24 hours by default."
fix:
Do not rely on retention shrinkage alone — the auditor's arithmetic assumed a fixed 6h gap, but the request is built without an explicit flex interval so flexInterval defaults to repeatInterval and consecutive runs can be ~12h apart, plus Doze deferral on top. Three changes:

1. PalmAstroApp.kt:71-79 — pin the flex and stop relying solely on the periodic schedule. Build the periodic request with an explicit short flex, e.g. PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<ScanImageCleanupWorker>(6, TimeUnit.HOURS, 15, TimeUnit.MINUTES), and additionally enqueue a OneTimeWorkRequest for ScanImageCleanupWorker (no initial delay, enqueueUniqueWork with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP) from onCreate, so every app launch sweeps immediately. That is what actually bounds the window in practice, since the app is opened far more often than every 24h.

2. PalmAstroApp.kt:77 — switch ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP to UPDATE. Note the auditor's suggestion to "bump the app version" does nothing here: KEEP is honored regardless of versionCode, so UPDATE (or a new WORK_NAME) is the only way an already-enqueued schedule picks up the new interval/flex.

3. ScanImageCleanupWorker.kt:74 — reduce RETENTION_MS to leave real margin, e.g. 20 * 60 * 60 * 1000L, which combined with (1) keeps the observed deletion comfortably inside the stated 24h.

Add the unit test the auditor asked for (app/src/test/kotlin/com/palmastro/app/worker/ScanImageCleanupWorkerTest.kt) asserting a file with lastModified() at now-21h is deleted and one at now-19h is not, so the constant and the disclosure stay coupled.

Separately worth noting while in this file: turning the retention switch off in Settings (SettingsViewModel.kt:106-109) also does not delete anything until the next worker run, while privacy_policy_en.html:65 says photos "are not kept after analysis" in that mode. The one-shot enqueue from (1) should also be fired from setRetention(false) to make that sentence true.
userImpact: The retention guarantee shown to users and declared to Google Play is not met: palm photographs remain on the device for up to six hours past the stated deletion deadline. A reviewer or regulator comparing the stated window against observed behavior finds the disclosure inaccurate.

There is no cleanup at Application.onCreate, at scan completion, or at settings change, so nothing shortens the gap. Capture writes to filesDir/scans/<monthKey>/<ANGLE>.jpg (ScanViewModel.kt:196-199), so mtime really is capture time and the staleness model is correct.
